blogs.author: Matt Zerweck
blogs.description: How legal teams are transforming their departments with Harvey to better serve the enterprise and help the business move faster.
blogs.content: Insights Building a Frontier In-House Organization How legal teams are transforming their departments with Harvey to better serve the enterprise and help the business move faster. by Matt Zerweck and Gabe Pereyra • Oct 13, 2026 Satya Nadella describes the frontier firm as a company built around intelligence on demand, where people and agents work side by side. Inside most companies, the legal department is where that shift arrives first. For the general counsels we work with, the question used to be how to get lawyers to use AI. Now it’s how to run the department on it. Behind that shift are four challenges we hear from in-house teams: Legal as the bottleneck. Lawyers spend too much time on work that doesn’t need legal judgment, instead of working at the top of their license. Rising volume, flat headcount. Demand for Legal grows with the business but headcount and budgets do not. Reactive instead of proactive. Regulatory change and contract risk surface late, when they’re already problems. No portfolio visibility. Contract history, obligations, and outside matters are scattered across systems, inboxes, and law firms. None of these problems stay in one lane. A single contract can be a bottleneck, a capacity problem, and a visibility gap at once. And when requests queue up and the business can’t see where they stand, employees bypass Legal and take legal questions to general-purpose AI tools, outside Legal’s controls. Banning that doesn't work. The frontier move is to give the business a better place to ask, with Legal in control of the answers. The Platform for a Frontier Legal Department Figure 1. The legal department of a frontier firm with everything in one place. We’re building Harvey as one platform for the business, its legal team, and outside counsel. It connects every request, contract, and matter with the documents, conversations, and context behind it. That knowledge, including the department’s policies, prior decisions, and outcomes, is codified in one legal brain that people and agents draw on as they work. Legal decides what agents can handle and where people should make the call. Legal puts that knowledge to work across requests, contracts, and matters. It sets what agents can handle, where people make the call, and when to involve outside counsel. Past matters, outcomes, and invoice data help Legal choose the right firm for the work. Requests come in and follow-up questions, updates, and completed work go back through the channels the business already uses. Each outcome adds to the department’s knowledge, informing the next decision. Figure 2. The platform architecture. Connected systems feed a shared model of the department’s work, with source permissions preserved. Harvey’s products and agents draw on that same model. If a sales lead asks whether a customer deal can include a new AI-use clause, Harvey can pull up the original request, the department’s position on AI clauses, the terms the company has agreed to before, and the EU rules that apply, all in one answer. We've built that connectivity with partners over several years. Harvey runs on Microsoft Azure and works inside Microsoft 365 , from Word to Copilot Cowork. It connects to LexisNexis for primary law, to Docusign and Ironclad for contract workflows, and through the Connector Library to the rest of the systems the department already uses. Resolve Requests Wherever the Business Works Intake extends the department’s legal front door across email, chat, and business systems, including Outlook, Gmail, Slack, Teams, Jira, ServiceNow, and Salesforce. Harvey gathers context, then routes and assigns work by type, risk, and department. Agents and lawyers send follow-up questions, updates, and completed work back through the same channels. Figure 3. Three paths for a request, with Legal setting the rules. Answers and completed work return to the business. Adapted from Winston Weinberg’s FORUM New York in-house keynote. blogs.content: Company Harvey to Open Tokyo Office by Harvey Team • Oct 12, 2026 Harvey will open an office in Tokyo in early 2027, deepening our commitment to supporting law firms and in-house legal teams in Japan. Trust is earned over time through close collaboration and consistent support. As we grow in Japan, we are investing in a local presence to build lasting relationships, listen to our customers, and ensure their needs guide how we continue to build and grow here. Our Tokyo office will support our growing customer base in Japan and deepen relationships with law firms including Mori Hamada & Matsumoto and Nagashima Ohno & Tsunematsu, and in-house legal teams, including Mitsubishi Corporation. A local presence will help us work more closely with these teams and strengthen the support we provide. We are also building Harvey to better support work in Japanese and reflect the needs of legal professionals in Japan. This includes our partnership with Legalscape for Japanese legal research. Working with local experts and listening to customer feedback will help guide how we develop our product and support its use. “Japan is a critical market for legal and home to many exceptional law firms and companies. With the government investing in AI acceleration country-wide, there’s no better time to bring Harvey to Tokyo,” said Winston Weinberg, Harvey’s Chief Executive Officer. “Having a team in Japan will help us better understand the needs of legal professionals in Japan and make their experience central to how we build and grow here.” Koji Toshima, Partner and CFO, Mori Hamada & Matsumoto, said, “Since establishing our partnership with Harvey in 2024, we have worked closely together to explore how AI can enhance the quality and efficiency of legal services in Japan. Harvey’s decision to open a Tokyo office is a very welcome and significant milestone, demonstrating its strong commitment to the Japanese legal market. Building on our collaboration to date, including our recent support in bringing about the partnership between Harvey and Legalscape, we look forward to further strengthening our collaboration with Harvey to advance the development of innovative AI solutions tailored to the needs of Japanese legal practice and deliver even greater value to our clients in Japan and around the world.” Tokyo will expand Harvey’s existing presence across Asia-Pacific, alongside our teams in Sydney, Singapore, and Bengaluru. Globally, more than 3,500 customers in over 85 countries use Harvey. We are grateful for the trust our customers in Japan have placed in us and look forward to building on our work here, alongside the lawyers and legal teams we serve. This guide provides information on our update cadence and links to vLex release notes so you can learn about new Vincent features. Summary Review the latest Vincent updates . This guide provides information on our update cadence and links to release notes so you can learn about new Vincent features and ensure you are getting the most out of the platform. Why This is Important Vincent is constantly evolving. As an AI engineered for lawyers , our platform is regularly enhanced with new capabilities and improvements. Staying informed about these updates allows you to leverage the latest tools and continuously improve your legal workflows. Our Update Cadence Vincent receives updates at the speed of AI. Our product and engineering teams work in a continuous development cycle. This means: Major Releases: We roll out major new features and capabilities in seasonal releases (e.g., Spring, Winter). Model Upgrades: We are constantly evaluating and implementing the latest-generation models from leading providers like OpenAI and Anthropic to ensure Vincent's responses are always clear, precise, and analytical. Latest Major Update: The Spring '25 Release Our most recent major update introduced a suite of powerful new capabilities designed to enhance your productivity and strategic insights. Key highlights include: New Workflow Engine: A new agentic AI framework that allows Vincent to reason about which tools to use for complex legal tasks, making the experience feel more like collaborating with an expert colleague. In this series, LegalOn CEO Daniel Lewis sits down with in-house legal professionals to talk workload, tools, trade-offs, and what it means to be a lawyer today. "A lean, tech-enabled team can handle far more internally. In under 18 months, we’ve cut more than $1 million in outside counsel spend while taking on more than ever." — Carlo Ciccarelli, Group General Counsel When Carlo Ciccarelli joined Lutech as Group General Counsel, the company—a 6,000-person leader in digital transformation—relied heavily on external firms for day-to-day legal support. Carlo had a clear mandate: reverse that pattern. He believed a leaner, tech-enabled in-house team could move faster and manage more work internally than the company had ever thought possible. To execute this vision, Carlo brought on Giorgia Frisina as Group Deputy Chief Legal Counsel Operations. Together, they rebuilt the function around a new philosophy: stop relying on outside firms for everyday work and instead use technology to give a small team massive leverage. The result? In less than 18 months, they have cut more than $1 million in outside counsel spend while dramatically expanding the scope and capability of their in-house team. A Team Built for Leverage Today, Lutech's legal group includes 23 people across legal and compliance. Outside counsel still has a role, but it is more targeted: specialized consultations and complex disputes rather than everyday work that can be handled inside the company. That shift requires more than hiring lawyers. It requires a way for the business to reach legal efficiently, and a way for legal to decide what needs attention, who should handle it, and what can be answered quickly. The team has recently launched its own internal intake and triage system. It gathers requests from the business, routes them to the right people, and begins generating answers and responses. That is not just AI at the edges of legal work. It is a different way for legal demand to enter the function in the first place. They do not have licenses for everyone, partly because of cost, and they are still in an experimentation mindset as they test what each system can do. With the complexity and scope of their international business, they’re looking for AI tools that fit their diverse needs. blogs.title: How Much of the Change Management Journey Does the Vendor Own?
blogs.author: Shadi
blogs.description: A conversation with Jerry Levine (Leah), Colin Levy (Malbek) and Rich Robinson (Epiq) Change management is an essential part of getting buy-in and ROI from legal technology investments. The gap between promise and outcome is already showing up in the numbers: legal AI adoption reached 78% in 2026, up from just 23% in 2023, yet […] The post How Much of the Change Management Journey Does the Vendor Own? appeared first on CLOC .
blogs.content: A conversation with Jerry Levine (Leah), Colin Levy (Malbek) and Rich Robinson (Epiq) Change management is an essential part of getting buy-in and ROI from legal technology investments. The gap between promise and outcome is already showing up in the numbers: legal AI adoption reached 78% in 2026 , up from just 23% in 2023, yet actual time savings from these tools have averaged 18.3% against a median vendor projection of 41% , according to research from the Legal Stack. Clearly, more change management is needed to support ROI expectations. But where does “vendor support” end and organizational change management begin? What is it reasonable for buyers to expect from a vendor, and what requires wider, enterprise change? We put the questions to three leaders who sit in different seats – a CLM platform, an e-discovery managed-services provider, and a legal AI company – and let them talk it through. What follows is an edited version of that conversation. No vendor can own transformation on behalf of the customer RICH ROBINSON (Epiq): I think the best vendors help organizations navigate change. What they can’t do is own transformation on behalf of the customer. We can provide the methodology, training, coaching, governance, and measurement. The organization still has to bring the leadership, accountability, and willingness to work differently. In my experience, the implementations that hold up are the ones where both sides share ownership of the journey. JERRY LEVINE (Leah): That’s a useful distinction to draw out, because my role isn’t what Rich just described, and I think buyers often assume every vendor is offering some version of it. Someone in a role like Rich’s delivers a change management program as part of what Epiq delivers. My role is different. I get adoption questions constantly, usually from a GC asking how to get people using the tool. I’ll talk it through with them. What I offer is guidance. You need someone internally, often externally too, who owns that work. COLIN LEVY (Malbek): I’d put myself closer to Jerry on that spectrum than to Rich. Malbek is a software vendor, not a managed-services business. Buyers want a partner now, not just a system. In my experience, that shows up as co-building the product with the customer, and staying in the relationship well past the sale. None of that is change management. It’s what separates a good vendor from one who shows up for the sale and disappears. If neither side has the resources, bring in a third party RICH: That’s why I think it’s important that whoever is running the selection and deployment process goes in with eyes open. You have to be honest about your own resources and about your vendor’s resources. Change management is critical to adoption. If neither side has the acumen or the bandwidth for it, my advice is to hire a third-party implementation partner rather than hope the gap closes on its own. JERRY: That gap is where things fall apart in practice. A customer comes back and asks how to get adoption going, and the honest answer depends on questions that often don’t have consistent answers inside the same organization. What have you done so far? Who’s driving this, and who just signed off on it? If leadership is pushing AI initiatives from the top down without knowing why, those initiatives are going to keep failing, and it won’t be the tool to blame. The “easy button” myth, and its mirror image on the vendor side RICH: I see this from both sides now that I’ve moved to the vendor side. Too many buyers treat these tools as an “easy button.” They’re not thinking about the time it takes to implement and deploy them, and especially the time it takes to get lawyers to change how they work. From the vendor’s side, there’s a mirror-image problem: a feeling that adoption should be a “no-brainer.” So hesitation reads as friction, not a real concern

blogs.content: Back to Blog GLM-Legal: Advancing Agentic Legal Intelligence Model By AutoClaw Team Oct 13 2026 Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, GLM-Legal matches frontier models on mainstream legal benchmarks.Designed for real legal workflows: contract review, evidence analysis, compliance, and more. Join the GLM-Legal Beta Whether you are a law firm, a legal tech company, an in-house legal team, or an independent practitioner, we invite you to experience GLM-Legal. - Apply for API access: https://z.ai/consultation/legal - Try AutoClaw: https://autoclaw.z.ai/ Large language models are shifting from single-turn code generation toward broader professional collaboration (Professional Cowork). Real-world knowledge work introduces distinct requirements: models must digest fragmented source files under concrete objectives and tight delivery constraints, structure specialized knowledge into cohesive analysis, and maintain domain rigor across the full execution lifecycle. Legal work concentrates on these challenges, providing an ideal stress test for training models to operate in high-stakes professional environments. Legal practice demands an unbroken chain between facts, statutory doctrine, analytical reasoning, and client-ready work product. When given a professional task, an agent must extract core issues from source documents, build defensible arguments, and format its findings to exact task specifications. Simultaneously satisfying all of these constraints is the true benchmark for domain-specific models. We evaluated GLM-Legal across three axes: complex task execution, specialized legal reasoning, and real-world legal workflows. GLM-Legal achieved a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey LAB, while matching frontier closed-source models on LegalBench and PLawBench despite running on a significantly leaner parameter footprint. Benchmark Highlights Across complex execution, legal reasoning, and real-world drafting, GLM-Legal matches frontier-tier performance while maintaining high inference efficiency: Harvey LAB (19.2% All-Pass Rate): In real-world law firm workflows across 24 practice areas, GLM-Legal scores 19.2% and improves on its base model by 12.5 percentage points. Under Harvey's strict all-pass grading, this confirms reliable end-to-end task execution without intermediate degradation. LegalBench (Domain Reasoning Parity): Parses specialized contracts, merger filings, and judicial opinions with the precision of top closed-source frontier models, despite operating on a significantly leaner parameter budget. PLawBench (Chinese Localized Practice): Achieves parity with leading frontier systems on Chinese legal consultation, case analysis, and document drafting under fine-grained rubrics. The results on the Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark and LegalBench were independently evaluated by Vals. See https://www.vals.ai/models/zai_glm-legal. Training Methodology GLM-Legal prioritizes training efficiency. Built on the lightweight GLM-5.3-Flash foundation, it scales domain competence through specialized mid-training coupled with high-efficiency post-training. By tying foundational pre-training directly to downstream task execution, we train the model to parse source records, apply doctrine, structure arguments, and maintain output quality through final delivery. 1. Mid-training: Solidifying Domain Foundations Mid-training establishes a systematic legal foundation. We expanded the volume of high-quality legal corpora, allowing the model to learn legal concepts, statutory rules, and interpretive frameworks within dense domain context. This stage strengthens deductive connections between facts, rules, and conclusions, providing the knowledge substrate required for complex downstream execution. 2. Post-training: Co-evolving the Model and Agent Harness Post-training translates domain knowledge into task execution via reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of realistic legal environments. blogs.description: Latest updates to ChatGPT and Codex
blogs.content: $ npm install -g @openai/codex@0.164.0 View details New Features Save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered /presets slots, with a keyboard menu for quick access. ( #54380 , #54381 ) Set model, reasoning effort, speed, and permission profiles directly with inline /model and /permissions arguments. ( #54378 , #54383 ) Preview viewed and generated images in the fullscreen transcript on terminals supporting Kitty or Sixel graphics. ( #54216 ) Authenticate enterprise MCP connections using eligible Codex account grants or dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients requiring secrets. ( #55334 , #55859 , #56001 ) Mask credentials during supported remote Bash commands and Zsh snapshot sessions, including credentials from custom providers. ( #54309 , #54432 , #56049 ) The Amazon Bedrock setup wizard is now enabled by default, with API key entry grouped alongside other AWS sign-in methods when credentials are detected. ( #56033 , #56023 ) Bug Fixes Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. ( #53932 , #55581 ) Resuming sessions now finds compressed histories and restores saved thread settings instead of replacing them with global defaults. ( #54008 , #55923 ) Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. ( #55994 , #56000 ) CLI configuration overrides are preserved when -c or --config appears at multiple subcommand levels. ( #56022 ) Queued prompts now wait for pending permission selections to resolve before continuing. ( #55682 ) Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. ( #54273 , #55384 ) Chores Reduced disk usage by pruning unused installations, cleaning abandoned marketplace checkouts, and bounding daemon logs. ( #53827 , #55149 , #55689 , #55690 , #55856 ) Updated the embedded JavaScript runtime with safety checks for optimized Array.sort operations. ( #54519 ) Changelog Full Changelog: rust-v0.163.0...rust-v0.164.0 #53725 Render Markdown web links as labels in Rex @bc-openai #53728 Preserve the remote cwd filter in the in-app resume picker @fcoury-oai #53732 Reuse compiled search patterns across compressed rollouts @ethernetdan-openai #53733 Default Guardian v2 async classification to conversation mode @felixxia-oai #53736 Acquire and cache opt-in executor capability inventories via V2 @TAFOYA-OAI #53745 Remove modelSlug from the latest-model resolver output @kkahadze-oai #53747 Prefer remote Visualize installs over the bundled plugin @philipp-oai #53751 Apply feature overrides when restarting the app-server daemon @jif-oai #53753 Extend copy-on-select to composer text @fcoury-oai #53754 Support Command/Super shortcuts in the TUI keymap @fcoury-oai #53763 Enrich V2 capability discovery with resolved plugin and skill metadata @TAFOYA-OAI #53780 Remove redundant Codex manual cache directory check @kkahadze-oai #53781 Remove the product-gating TODO from SkillPolicy @kkahadze-oai #53784 Forward client voice session IDs in realtime requests @chrisdong-oai #53790 Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts @bz-openai #53794 Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation @jif-oai #53795 Use the bundled model catalog in the MCP startup invalidation test @OLI-OAI #53797 Refresh Guardian reviews when review context changes @jif-oai #53800 Wire background compaction into the turn lifecycle @rka-oai #53804 Keep the Agent command center visible during archive and delete @etraut-openai #53805 Add safe diagnostics to workspace routing configuration errors @etraut-openai #53811 Support daemon installation from Windows WinGet packages @etraut-openai #53816 Reject Guardian review threads during interactive CLI resume @dylan-hurd-oai #53827 Prune unused app-server daemon releases safely @etraut-openai #53831 Track content provenance through prompt ass

blogs.content: What's New Week 37 · September 7–11, 2026 Copy page Copy page Test your plugins with claude plugin eval and pop Claude Code Desktop panes out into their own windows. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.263 → v2.1.269 2 features · September 7–11 Test plugins with claude plugin eval v2.1.269 claude plugin eval runs your plugin against a suite of test cases, scores the results, and by default runs each case again without the plugin so you can see what it contributes. claude plugin eval init asks you what a good result looks like, then proposes test cases and the checks that score them, tries the suite once, and writes the files. Every run, and every check that has a second model judge the reply, is a real model call on your account. From your plugin’s root directory, have Claude draft the suite: terminal claude plugin eval init When Claude tells you the suite is ready, exit the session that claude plugin eval init opened and run claude plugin eval . to score every case. The summary table prints in your terminal, and report.html under evals/results/ has the per-run detail. Test plugins with evals Pop Desktop panes out into their own windows Desktop In the Claude Code Desktop app, you can pop any pane out into its own window. Drag the diff or terminal to a second screen while Claude keeps working in the main window, then dock the pane back when you’re done. Arrange your workspace Other wins Set maxEffortLevel at the top level or per model under modelSettings to cap the effort level on every provider, including Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry; any higher level runs at the cap Point --plugin-dir at a folder of plugins to load each immediate subfolder that has a manifest If WebFetch hasn’t finished downloading a page within five minutes, the fetch fails with a deadline error instead of hanging; set CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_DEADLINE_MS to change the deadline, or to 0 to remove the limit Pass --json to claude plugin install , uninstall , update , enable , or disable to print the result as one JSON object on the last line of stdout When the auto mode classifier blocks an action, the reason Claude receives usually names the rule that matched , such as [Data Exfiltration] When you type / partway through a prompt, you can now pick from a list of matching commands instead of a single suggestion. The list opens as you type in fullscreen rendering. A plugin skill also matches on its name without the plugin prefix In the VS Code extension, click the agent count at the bottom of the prompt box to open the agent map , where you can open a subagent’s read-only transcript or stop it In the VS Code extension, select Hooks or Permissions in the command menu’s Customize section to add or remove hooks and permission rules in your user, project, and local settings Claude can pick a browser-tab icon to match each artifact it publishes In Claude Code on the web, take back a queued message in a cloud session before Claude reads it: remove it from the queue, or press Esc or Up , and the text returns to the message box Full changelog for v2.1.263–v2.1.269 → Was this page helpful? Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.240 → v2.1.250 3 features · August 24–28 Resume terminal sessions in the Desktop app Desktop Type /resume in the Claude Code Desktop prompt box to pick up any session you started from the CLI and continue it in the app with the full conversation and context intact. Search your sessions by title, folder, or branch, and preview where you left off before you resume. In a Desktop session, run the command to list your terminal sessions: Claude Code > /resume Select a session and press Enter . The conversation opens in the app where you left off. Move between the CLI and Desktop Claude-drafted feedback CLI When a tool keeps failing, Claude can’t help with a request, or you point out a mistake, Claude now drafts a feedback report for you with the SendFeedback tool. A card above your prompt shows the draft, and you can review, send, or dismiss it from there. Nothing reaches Anthropic until you send it. Requires v2.1.238 or later. Run /feedback with no argument to open your queue of drafts from every session: Claude Code > /feedback Select a draft, then edit, send, or discard it. To turn drafting off, set Claude-drafted feedback to off in /config . SendFeedback tool behavior Restricted mode v2.1.248 Restricted mode starts Claude Code without the built-in tools that run commands or code. Use it when an evaluation harness drives claude on a shared machine. Start it with --restricted or set CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1 . Claude Code also removes WebFetch , confines the file tools to the working directories, loads only managed settings and --settings , and refuses the bypassPermissions permission mode. Run a non-interactive query without the command-running tools: terminal claude --restricted -p "review src/ for SQL injection risks" To give Claude one of the removed tools back, list it in --tools together with the other built-in tools you want, for example --tools "Bash,Read,Edit" . --tools is an allowlist, and its default preset doesn’t restore the removed tools. blogs.content: What's New Week 34 · August 17–21, 2026 Copy page Copy page Draft editable UI artboards with the /design skill, set the Concise output style, and start a Claude Code session on your machine from your phone. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.234 → v2.1.239 3 features · August 17–21 /design research preview The /design skill brings Claude Design’s artboard workflow into the CLI and Claude Code Desktop, built on artifacts. Run it with a brief and Claude publishes a canvas of editable artboards for your UI. Pick one, tweak it, then have Claude implement it. Available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. Requires v2.1.234 or later. Describe what you want designed and let Claude draft the options: Claude Code > /design redesign the composer based on what people actually use it for Claude prints a link to the published canvas. Open it, pick an artboard, and tell Claude which option to implement. Where artifacts are available Concise output style v2.1.237 Concise is a new built-in output style. Claude leads with the result and skips preamble and narration, while doing the work as thoroughly as in the Default style. When you ask for an explanation or more detail, Claude answers in full. Error reports, security warnings, and confirmations for destructive actions keep their complete content. Turn it on under Output style in /config , or set it in your settings file: ~/.claude/settings.json { "outputStyle" : "Concise" } Run /clear or start a new session, and Claude’s replies lead with the result. Built-in output styles Start a session on your machine from your phone mobile Any machine running claude remote-control now shows up as a device card at the top of the Code tab in the Claude app. Remote Control is also out of research preview. Start Remote Control on the machine you want to reach, then open the Code tab on your phone: terminal claude remote-control Your machine appears as a device card at the top of the Code tab. Tap it to pick a directory and start a session there. Start a Remote Control session Other wins Claude Code now continues your session automatically when a claude.ai usage limit resets; turn it off from the Continue automatically at usage limit row in /config The optional spellcheck setting underlines misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using your installed aspell , hunspell , or ispell On a branch with an open GitLab merge request, with the glab CLI authenticated through glab auth login , the footer shows an MR !N badge colored by whether the merge request is a draft, open, or mergeable Change the effort level from your phone or claude.ai/code and it applies to the session on your machine ; set CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0 to opt out Your own prompts now render markdown in the transcript, with highlighted code blocks, inline code, and lists, the same way replies do The new ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL environment variable sets the model new sessions start on; blogs.description: Claude Code Desktop auto-continues after a usage limit resets, fork mode turns on by default, and GitLab merge requests and marketplaces join GitHub.
blogs.content: What's New Week 33 · August 10–14, 2026 Copy page Copy page Claude Code Desktop auto-continues after a usage limit resets, fork mode turns on by default, and GitLab merge requests and marketplaces join GitHub. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.225 → v2.1.233 3 features · August 10–14 Auto-continue after a usage limit on Desktop Desktop When you hit your session limit in the Code tab of Claude Code Desktop, the limit card now offers an Auto-continue when limits reset checkbox. Check it, and the Desktop app retries the interrupted turn after the reset. The card shows the retry time. The weekly-limit card doesn’t offer it. The next time a session-limit card appears, check Auto-continue when limits reset and leave the session open. The card shows Auto-resuming at followed by the reset time, and the turn picks up on its own once the limit resets. What to do when you hit a usage limit Fork mode on by default v2.1.232 Fork mode is now on by default in interactive sessions. Claude can request the fork subagent type, which inherits the full conversation and prompt cache instead of starting fresh, so you don’t have to re-explain the context for a side task. Subagents Claude spawns in interactive sessions, apart from the ones an agent-team teammate spawns, also run in the background by default. Start a fork yourself with a task that needs everything you’ve discussed so far: Claude Code > /subtask draft unit tests for the parser changes so far The fork appears in the panel below your prompt and its result arrives in your conversation when it finishes. To turn fork mode off, set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 . Turn fork mode on or off GitLab merge requests and marketplaces v2.1.232 Plugin marketplaces clone bare gitlab.com URLs, including nested subgroups. On v2.1.233 or later, pass a GitLab merge request URL to --worktree to branch from it, and the claude agents view labels sessions linked to a merge request as !N . Claude Code also redacts GitLab token families such as glpat- and glrt- , and protects the glab CLI’s config store the same way it protects gh . Start a session in a worktree branched from a merge request: terminal claude --worktree https://gitlab.com/group/project/-/merge_requests/42 When origin is on gitlab.com, Claude Code fetches merge-requests/42/head and opens the session on that branch in its own worktree. Branch a worktree from a pull or merge request Other wins Type @ in the prompt to mention another Claude session by name, and Claude messages it directly with SendMessage ; a bare name that matches exactly one live session now delivers without a confirmation step Interactive sessions on one machine keep unique names : if you start or rename a session with a name another live session already uses, Claude Code gives yours a name-word-word variant and tells you Plugin marketplaces accept command sources : a local command prints the plugin directory, which Claude Code re-resolves each session and applies without a restart On Linux and WSL, set CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT to a size such as 4G to cap the memory Bash and PowerShell tool commands can use The task-tracking tools, such as TaskCreate , TaskUpdate , and TodoWrite , are no longer available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and later models in those families ; set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 to re-enable them /code-review at high, xhigh, and max effort now runs in a background agent like the other levels /plugin install plugin@marketplace refreshes the marketplace first, so newly published plugins install without a manual marketplace update Settings accept additionalMarketplaces and allowedMarketplaces as aliases for extraKnownMarketplaces and strictKnownMarketplaces On newer models, Claude can overwrite an existing file with the Write tool without reading it first this session, matching the Edit tool’s rules; older models require the read The VS Code extension can organize the sessions list into groups : right-click to create, rename, or delete a group

blogs.description: Claude Code sessions message each other, self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your infrastructure, and auto mode becomes the default permission mode.
blogs.content: What's New Week 32 · August 3–7, 2026 Copy page Copy page Claude Code sessions message each other, self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your infrastructure, and auto mode becomes the default permission mode. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.220 → v2.1.224 3 features · August 3–7 Cross-session messaging v2.1.224 Your Claude Code sessions can now message each other. Claude discovers your other sessions with the ListAgents tool and sends with SendMessage , either when you ask it to or on its own, such as after a change in one session affects what another is working on. A message is text Claude writes for the other session, never your conversation history or files. Available on macOS and Linux. Requires v2.1.224 or later. With two sessions open on the same machine, ask one of them to pass something along: Claude Code Tell the session working on the payments API that users.name is now users.display_name The other session shows a Message from row once Claude has read the message; press Ctrl+O to expand it. To see which sessions Claude can reach, run /list-agents . Message another session Self-hosted environments v2.1.224 Self-hosted environments run Claude Code cloud sessions on your organization’s own infrastructure, in public beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Run claude self-hosted-runner on your machines or containers to turn them into runners. When someone picks your environment while starting a session from claude.ai, the mobile or desktop apps, or claude --cloud , that session runs inside your network, with access to your internal services. An Owner turns on Allow self-hosted environments in admin settings first. Signed in as an Owner, run the guided setup, which walks you through creating the environment and starts a runner: terminal claude self-hosted-runner setup The environment shows Healthy in admin settings once the runner registers. Self-hosted environments quickstart Auto mode becomes the default CLI Starting August 14, auto mode is the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. If you set a default mode yourself, it stays in place unless you accept the one-time switch prompt, and a default your organization manages doesn’t change. You can still switch modes at any time. Already in effect on those plans: the classifier calls auto mode makes no longer count toward your usage limits. To start every session in auto mode before the switch, set it as your default in your user settings: ~/.claude/settings.json { "permissions" : { "defaultMode" : "auto" } } New sessions then show auto mode on in the status bar. blogs.content: What's New Week 30 · July 20–24, 2026 Copy page Copy page Opus 5 becomes the default Opus model, Claude Code Desktop adds an iOS Simulator pane, and the Claude Security plugin scans your code for vulnerabilities. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.214 → v2.1.219 3 features · July 20–24 Claude Opus 5 new model Claude Opus 5 is the new default Opus model in Claude Code. It’s the default on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and the Anthropic API, and on Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform. On the Anthropic API and on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, Opus 5 runs with a 1M-token context window ; on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, select the 1M model variant. Fast mode moves to Opus 5 at $10/$50 per MTok. Requires v2.1.219 or later. Switch to Opus 5 by name, or pick it from the model picker: Claude Code > /model claude-opus-5 Model configuration iOS Simulator in Claude Code Desktop Desktop Claude Code Desktop on macOS gets an iOS Simulator pane, in public beta on Pro, Max, and Team plans. When Claude builds, launches, or checks your app in a simulator, the pane opens next to the conversation and streams the device screen live, so you can watch Claude tap through the app to verify its changes or drive the device yourself. Requires Xcode with the iOS platform installed, and Claude Desktop v1.24012.0 or later. Ask Claude to run or test your app, and the pane opens when the app launches: Claude Code > Build the app and run it in the simulator to check the onboarding flow. Test iOS apps in the simulator Claude Security plugin plugin The Claude Security plugin runs a multi-agent vulnerability scan of your codebase inside a Claude Code session: agents map your architecture, build a threat model, hunt for vulnerabilities, and independently review every finding before writing the report to a CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ directory. Scan a whole repository or only a branch’s diff, a pull request, or a single commit, then turn the findings you choose into reviewed patches that you apply yourself. Install the plugin from the official Anthropic marketplace, run /reload-plugins , then start a scan with /claude-security : Claude Code > /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official Scan and fix your codebase Other wins /code-review now runs as a background subagent with its own context window, so review work stays out of your conversation and the findings arrive when it completes /verify , /code-review , and /deep-research run only when you invoke them; Claude no longer launches them on its own Emoji shortcodes autocomplete in the prompt input: type :heart: to insert an emoji, or two or more characters after : for suggestions; turn it off with emojiCompletionEnabled Skills with context: fork run in the background by default, and background: false in the skill’s frontmatter waits for the result in the same turn A session runs up to 20 subagents concurrently by default; change the limit with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS --max-budget-usd now enforces the cap on subagents: once spend reaches it, Claude can’t start more and running background subagents stop New sandbox.filesystem.disabled setting skips filesystem isolation while keeping network egress control In auto mode, the checks for dangerous rm commands, background jobs, and suspicious Windows paths no longer open permission dialogs; the auto-mode classifier adjudicates them instead Bash permission checks fail closed on more shell forms, including file-descriptor redirects, Zsh variable subscripts in [[ ]] comparisons, help and man invocations that could run unsafe options, and commands over 10,000 characters Fast mode no longer supports Opus 4.7: /fast now applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 Long-running tool calls emit a periodic progress heartbeat instead of going silent Full changelog for v2.1.214–v2.1.219 → Was this page helpful? blogs.title: 官方报告怎么做成可编辑 PPT？AutoClaw 实操案例
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: 以国家统计局《2025年国民经济和社会发展统计公报》为例，介绍如何用 AutoClaw 把官方长报告整理成 12 页可编辑 PPT，并同步生成逐页讲稿、图表来源表和原文证据对应…
blogs.content: 返回博客 官方报告怎么做成可编辑 PPT？AutoClaw 实操案例 教程 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年10月23日 以国家统计局《2025年国民经济和社会发展统计公报》为例，介绍如何用 AutoClaw 把官方长报告整理成 12 页可编辑 PPT，并同步生成逐页讲稿、图表来源表和原文证据对应表。 把官方报告做成 PPT，难点不只是“缩短文字” 把一份几十页的官方报告做成可汇报的 PPT，通常要完成四件事：找出真正值得讲的数据，把数据改造成容易理解的图表，为每一页写好讲稿，还要保留来源，方便别人复核。只让 AI “总结成 PPT”，往往能得到一份看起来完整、但数据来源不清、图表无法编辑、上台也不知道怎么讲的文件。 更稳妥的做法，是把任务定义成一套完整交付： 可编辑 PPT、逐页讲稿、图表来源表、页面与原文证据对应表 。这次我们用 AutoClaw 处理国家统计局《2025年国民经济和社会发展统计公报》，最终得到一份 12 页 PPT、一份约 10 分钟的逐页讲稿，以及三份用于核验的来源文件。 先给结论：一份能真正拿去汇报的 PPT，需要五类交付物 交付物 解决的问题 12 页可编辑 PPT 文字、数字和图表可以继续修改，不是图片拼接 逐页讲稿 Word 告诉汇报人每页讲什么，控制整体时长 数据与图表来源表 说明每个数字和每张图来自哪里 PPT 页面与原文证据对应表 快速回到官方报告中的原始表述 官方来源清单 集中保存发布机构、页面链接和访问日期 这里最重要的不是文件数量，而是让“内容、表达和证据”同时交付。PPT 用于展示，讲稿用于表达，证据表用于复核，三者缺一块，后续都容易返工。 这个案例是怎么做的 第一步：限定唯一的一手来源 本次案例只使用国家统计局发布的《中华人民共和国 2025 年国民经济和社会发展统计公报》，没有用第三方文章补数字，也没有从网上随意找配图。来源页面发布于 2026 年 2 月 28 日，本次访问日期为 2026 年 10 月 23 日。 这样做的好处是，读者可以直接回到原文核验。代价是可用信息完全受官方公报范围限制，找不到的数据不能凭经验补齐。 第二步：先设计汇报结构，再开始做页面 长报告不适合按原文顺序逐段搬进 PPT。更合理的方式，是先确定听众最关心的问题，再把内容重新组织成“总览—分主题数据—结论”的结构。本案例把经济总量、人口与城镇化、就业与物价、居民收入、粮食生产、绿色发展等信息拆成 12 页，保证每一页只回答一个主要问题。 例如，经济总览页集中呈现国内生产总值 1401879 亿元、同比增长 5.0%，以及第三产业增加值占比 57.7%；居民收入页则单独呈现全国居民人均可支配收入 43377 元。信息被分开后，页面的重点更清楚，也更适合口头汇报。 第三步：用原始数据重绘可编辑图表 案例中的折线图、柱状图都依据公报数据重新绘制，图表元素可以继续编辑。这样做比直接截取网页图表更实用：汇报人可以调整颜色、字号、坐标轴和标注，也可以根据自己的时间删减页面。 图表页面同时保留来源说明，包括发布机构、报告名称、发布日期和访问日期。即使 PPT 被单独转发，接收者也能判断数据来自哪里。 第四步：同步写逐页讲稿 这份 12 页 PPT 同步生成了约 1900 字的逐页讲稿，建议汇报时长约 10 分钟。讲稿不是把页面文字再读一遍，而是补充页面之间的过渡、数字代表的含义，以及哪些结论只能谨慎表达。 如果演讲时间变化，也可以据此快速压缩。例如，5 分钟汇报可以保留总览、三个核心主题和结尾；10 分钟汇报则可以按完整讲稿展开。 第五步：建立页面与原文的对应关系 正式汇报最怕被问到“这个数字从哪里来的”。因此，本案例额外输出了 PPT 页面与原文证据对应表。表中记录页码、页面主题、所用数据、官方原文位置和来源链接。需要复核时，不必重新在长报告里搜索。 可以直接复用的任务描述 请把国家统计局《中华人民共和国 2025 年国民经济和社会发展统计公报》整理成一份适合 10 分钟汇报的可编辑 PPT。只使用国家统计局官方页面和官方报告中的信息，不使用第三方数据或网络图片。PPT 控制在 12 页左右，每页只表达一个主要结论，图表根据官方数据重新绘制并保持可编辑。请同时输出逐页讲稿、数据与图表来源表、PPT 页面与原文证据对应表，以及官方来源清单。所有具体数据都写明来源链接、发布日期和访问日期；找不到官方依据的内容不要补写。 换成其他行业报告时，只需要替换报告名称、汇报对象、页数和时长。来源要求、可编辑要求、讲稿要求和证据表要求建议保留。 交付前必须检查什么 数字是否一致。逐项核对 PPT、讲稿、来源表与官方原文，特别注意单位、百分比和同比口径。 图表是否可编辑。点击图表中的数据系列、标题和坐标轴，确认不是一张扁平图片。 结论是否超过原文。官方材料只说明事实时，不要把它扩写成因果判断。 来源是否能打开。检查链接、页面标题、发布机构、发布日期和访问日期。 讲稿是否与页面同步。删页或改数据后，讲稿和证据表也要一起更新。 这类任务的边界 本案例使用的是国家统计局公报中的初步统计数，后续可能修订。文章中的数字用于展示资料整理和演示文稿制作方法，不代替最新官方数据，也不构成经济分析结论。 AutoClaw 可以帮助完成资料读取、结构整理、图表制作、讲稿撰写和来源归档，但最终汇报人仍需确认数据口径、受众和表达尺度。涉及财务、法律、医疗或政策判断时，还需要对应领域人员复核。 常见问题 PDF 或网页报告也能转成 PPT 吗？ 可以，前提是内容能够正常读取。扫描版 PDF 可能需要先做文字识别，并人工检查表格和数字。 AI 生成的 PPT 是不是只能当草稿？ 如果只有页面文件，通常仍需要较多人工整理；如果同时产出讲稿、来源表和证据对应表，就更接近可直接修改和汇报的成品。 为什么一定要保留访问日期？ 网页内容可能更新。访问日期可以说明制作 PPT 时依据的是哪个时间点的页面信息。

blogs.description: Pull live data into published artifacts through MCP connectors, and use Claude Code with a screen reader in the new screen reader mode.
blogs.content: What's New Week 29 · July 13–17, 2026 Copy page Copy page Pull live data into published artifacts through MCP connectors, and use Claude Code with a screen reader in the new screen reader mode. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.207 → v2.1.212 2 features · July 13–17 Artifacts call your MCP connectors web A published artifact can now call MCP connectors each time someone views it, so a dashboard shows live data and can take actions on demand rather than a snapshot from the session that built it. Each call runs through the viewing account’s own connections, and viewers approve access before the page’s first connector call. This week also adds public sharing links, editor roles for shared editing on Team and Enterprise plans, and artifacts created from Claude Tag sessions. Name the connector and the data you want in your prompt: Claude Code Build a dashboard artifact of open pull requests that pulls the live list through my GitHub connector when the page loads. Pull live data with MCP connectors Screen reader mode CLI Screen reader mode replaces the visual terminal interface with plain, linear text: instead of boxes, spinners, and in-place redraws, Claude Code prints labeled lines that a screen reader such as VoiceOver or NVDA reads in order, so you can approve permissions and review output end to end. Turn it on per session with a flag, per shell with the CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER environment variable, or everywhere with the axScreenReader setting. Start a session in screen reader mode: terminal claude --ax-screen-reader Turn on screen reader mode Other wins /fork now copies your conversation into a new background session with its own row in claude agents while you keep working; the in-session forked subagent it used to launch is now /subtask Auto mode no longer needs the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE opt-in on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry; administrators can turn it off with disableAutoMode MCP tool calls that run longer than two minutes now move to the background automatically so the session stays usable; tune or disable the threshold with CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS New claude auto-mode reset restores the default auto-mode configuration, and --yes skips the confirmation prompt New corporate launcher support: CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER or the processWrapper setting runs the processes Claude Code starts from its own binary, such as the background service and agent view sessions, through a required wrapper executable vimInsertModeRemaps setting maps two-key insert-mode sequences such as jj to Escape in vim mode --forward-subagent-text and CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT include subagent text and thinking blocks in stream-json output Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION ”Always allow” permission rules save at the repository root, so approvals granted in a git worktree persist across sessions and worktrees Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Claude Platform on AWS now default to Claude Opus 4.8 The collapsed tool summary line shows a live elapsed-time counter, so long-running tool calls visibly tick instead of looking stuck Full changelog for v2.1.207–v2.1.212 → Was this page helpful? blogs.description: Browse external sites from the Desktop app's built-in browser, run a full setup checkup with /doctor, and pick up auto mode transcript protections and agent view upgrades.
blogs.content: What's New Week 28 · July 6–10, 2026 Copy page Copy page Browse external sites from the Desktop app’s built-in browser, run a full setup checkup with /doctor, and pick up auto mode transcript protections and agent view upgrades. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.202 → v2.1.206 2 features · July 6–10 In-app browser on Desktop Desktop Claude Code on desktop now has a built-in browser. Claude can pull up docs, designs, or any other site, and read, click through, and interact with pages the same way it does with your local dev server previews. The browser is sandboxed and configurable: you choose whether browsing sessions persist, and safety classifiers review actions on external sites. Browse external sites /doctor is a full setup checkup v2.1.205 /doctor now diagnoses issues and can fix them, instead of printing a read-only report. It checks installation health, finds unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones, proposes trimming CLAUDE.md content Claude could derive from the codebase, and flags slow hooks. It reports findings first and asks for confirmation before changing anything. /checkup is its alias. Run a checkup from any session: Claude Code > /doctor All commands Other wins Auto mode now blocks tampering with session transcript files, and asks before running rm -rf on a variable it can’t resolve from context /cd now suggests directory paths as you type, matching /add-dir /commit-push-pr auto-allows git push to the repo’s configured push remote in addition to origin Gateway: /login now supports Anthropic-operated public gateway endpoints EnterWorktree asks for confirmation before entering a git worktree outside the project’s .claude/worktrees/ directory Background agents upgrade to a new version in the background right after a Claude Code update, instead of paying a slow stale-session upgrade when you attach Agent view rows now show a colored state word and a classifier-written headline instead of raw tool call text, and sessions that edit, merge, comment on, or push to an existing PR link it in claude agents Auto-update binary downloads now stream to disk instead of buffering in memory, cutting the updater’s peak memory usage by roughly 400 MB Background task notifications now explicitly state that no human input has occurred, preventing fabricated in-transcript approvals from being acted on Improved /code-review findings quality on Opus 4.8 across all effort levels Full changelog for v2.1.202–v2.1.206 → Was this page helpful? blogs.title: v2.1.310
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled; long foreground sleeps are now blocked there too
  • Fixed requests failing behind some gateways and compatible servers that reject the effort-2025-11-24 beta value or mid-conversation system messages; Claude Code now retries without them
  • Fixed background cleanup deleting some recent files, such as pasted images, when cleanupPeriodDays is set to a very large value
  • Fixed compaction after a "Prompt is too long" error keeping too much of a conversation with dense text, such as base64 or SVG, so the next request could fail again
  • Fixed file read permission prompts not showing where a symbolic link leads
  • Fixed a question's auto-continue timeout firing the moment the external editor closed after a long edit
  • Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks letting a tool call through when Git Bash is missing and the hook's command is only quoted strings, such as a quoted path
  • Improved auto mode's prompt before the first read outside the working directories: it now says when blocking those reads makes shell commands ask for permission
  • Improved memory use of non-interactive sessions (-p, Agent SDK) during compaction when the transcript file is very large
  • Improved a mod's Image to draw inside tmux with allow-passthrough and focus-events on, in kitty, Ghostty, and iTerm2 3.5+ with fullscreen rendering, where it showed only its alt text
  • Linux: Improved /sandbox and the sandbox startup warning to name Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on user namespaces, and how to lift it, when it keeps bubblewrap from starting the sandbox
  • Changed the error for an MCP tool call that times out in a non-interactive session while the server's elicitation is unanswered: it now tells Claude that no answer came and not to repeat the call
  • [VSCode] Fixed pressing Enter on the plan review card's "Send feedback and keep planning" button approving the plan instead of sending your comments back
  • [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing "Something went wrong" after "Switch branch & continue" on a cloud session opened from Session history's Web tab
  • [Cloud sessions] Added Claude Code cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles, so Owners can control access to each by role
  • [Cloud sessions] Added a Choose file button to load a cloud environment's setup script from a file
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed saves and archives in the cloud environment edit dialog showing no error inside the dialog
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed routine API token actions showing only a toast; the error now appears in the routine edit dialog
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved the session start checklist to show a cloud environment's setup script output in a scrolling box
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed turning on Cloud sessions or Remote Control in admin settings to ask for confirmation and list the custom roles that have that permission
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed the cloud environment dialog to open network access, setup script and environment variables from rows instead of listing every editor at once
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag treating ! commands such as !restart and !help as ordinary messages when sent in bold, italic or strikethrough
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag admin channel and workspace pages being replaced by a load error when a background refresh of the bundle list fails
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag's spend limits page in admin settings reporting that no channels match a filter while channel names are still loading
  • [Code Review] Fixed the Code Review admin section hidi

blogs.title: v2.1.309
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
  • Fixed macOS sandbox denyWrite glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with --mcp-config
  • Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions
  • Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open
  • Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the cd is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain cd
  • Fixed an Edit(path) deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
  • Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
  • Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
  • Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from ! mode
  • Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
  • Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that jq could not parse
  • Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's /proc
  • Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed
  • Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization
  • Fixed the claude remote-control status line showing HEAD as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository
  • Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and --tools rules given on the leader's command line
  • Fixed sessions renamed with /rename appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive --resume
  • Fixed the /rewind list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through /code-review --fix, a subagent or a shell command
  • Fixed /privacy-settings showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched
  • Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug
  • Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript
  • Fixed a skill in an --add-dir folder being unreachable when another skill already held its name; it is now offered as :
  • Fixed /verify and /co

blogs.title: v2.1.307
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added /claude-api api-version to move Claude API code to API version 2026-10-21
  • Added the claude_code.safety_event OpenTelemetry event for each tool call a permission rule, auto mode, a safety check, a hook or the sandbox stopped, prompted or sent back
  • Fixed requests failing with a model-not-found error when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT is set and the model is an alias with the [1m] suffix, such as opus[1m]
  • Fixed the prompt-caching-scope beta header being sent behind custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateways and on Foundry, where it has no effect
  • Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in claude -p on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in
  • Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
  • Fixed HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call; only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried
  • Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
  • Fixed some "Autocompact is thrashing" errors in turns that read many PDF pages, images or other large tool results
  • Fixed /autocompact in cloud sessions going back to the default window after the session restarted
  • Fixed a conversation cleared with /clear sometimes coming back when a cloud or self-hosted runner session restarted
  • Fixed CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS being ignored in Claude apps gateway sessions
  • Fixed telemetry from Claude Desktop sessions behind a Claude apps gateway being rejected when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is set
  • Fixed /permissions > Recently denied not showing the denied shell command, and auto mode's local classifier ignoring an approval from there when it checks a retried command; approving a row now names the command, not its description
  • Fixed /help and the / command menu showing long model-facing descriptions for bundled skills such as /claude-api instead of their short descriptions
  • Fixed subagent transcripts recording placeholder token usage and an empty stop reason for streamed responses
  • Fixed model switches through the Agent SDK's setModel(), and apps built on it, being refused when the API took more than 5 seconds to confirm the model; Claude Code now waits up to 15 seconds
  • Fixed a background command stopped through a connected app (such as the desktop app archiving an idle session) being reported to Claude as stopped by the user; the notice now names its output file
  • Fixed WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions reporting a tool error when a site answered with a 4xx status or a robots.txt refusal; it is now a normal result, as in local sessions
  • Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab

  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with --use-anthropic-git-proxy committing a .claude/settings.local.json left in the clone by an earlier session
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session, or stopping the runner, during its checkout hook leaving the hook's processes running and the runner's slot held

blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces so sandboxed commands on Linux can create user namespaces (Chromium, rootless podman); this lets them get around the sandbox's file protections
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_USAGE_LIMIT_RECHECK_MS so unattended retry mode (CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG) notices a usage limit that was lifted before its reset
  • Fixed every request failing on Vertex, Bedrock and other providers when the endpoint or a gateway rejects tool search, and behind gateways with ToolSearch disallowed or left out of --tools (a 2.1.304 regression): Claude Code now retries without it
  • Fixed /effort and /autocompact settings not applying when the model name differed from a modelOverrides value by letter case or a [1m] tag
  • Fixed new worktrees in a bare repository sometimes starting from local HEAD instead of the default branch, and unchanged subagent worktrees sometimes not being cleaned up
  • Fixed Bash commands on a full disk failing with a raw ENOSPC file path: the error now says the disk is full and that nothing ran
  • Fixed an MCP server passed by a cloud session or by the SDK's setMcpServers being replaced later in the session by a same-named server from your own settings
  • Fixed Claude naming the wrong model for a subagent's work after the subagent switched to a fallback model
  • Fixed cloud sessions and teammates not telling Claude when a compaction had to leave the oldest messages out of its summary to fit
  • Fixed more cases of scheduled Cowork cloud sessions waiting five minutes for each subagent whose WebFetch needed a URL approval that nobody was there to give
  • Fixed Workflow resume re-running already-completed pipeline() and parallel() agents instead of serving them from the run's journal
  • Fixed Remote Control leaving empty "(session)" entries in /resume after switching conversations with /resume
  • Fixed /usage rows being cut off in narrow terminals
  • Fixed startup warnings printing as raw text above the logo: they now go to the debug log, and permission rules that restrict nothing show as warning rows under the banner
  • Fixed screen reader mode: search boxes now say "Search:" instead of a symbol VoiceOver read as "telephone recorder", and highlighted prompt text, such as Ctrl+R search matches and "ultrathink", no longer has spaces inside words
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed a start script that shares only its stdout with the runner or orchestrator failing with Resource temporarily unavailable when TERM is set (a 2.1.300 regression)
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed repository access failing since 2.1.296 when a git credential helper or askpass program reads its settings through GIT_CONFIG
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed the orchestrator reporting a spawn-runner hook as timed out when a runner it started in the background kept its output open
  • Improved /usage: each warning is now a one-line fix that names its source, and f applies the fixes; the same fixes appear in VS Code and /doctor
  • Improved MCP consent dialogs so an Enter meant for the prompt is less likely to be taken as Accept
  • Improved a mod's Image to draw its picture in iTerm2 3.5 and later with fullscreen rendering, where it showed only its alt text
  • Remote Control: Improved the spawn-mode messages: pressing w now says the new mode is saved for the folder, and a later claude remote-control start that uses the saved mode says where it came from
  • Changed allowedMcpServers to stop filtering managed-mcp.json stdio servers that

  • Fixed the organization policy not refreshing until the hourly check after approving an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at startup or switching "Use custom API key" in /config
  • Fixed sandboxed commands failing to start on Linux when a sandbox.filesystem.denyRead glob contains brackets that are not a character class, such as a [user-id] route folder

  • Fixed a claude.ai Directory plugin's skills not running as commands when picked from the "/" menu in Cowork cloud sessions
  • Fixed Remote Control permanently withholding a desktop conversation's history when a different account was signed in to the terminal
  • Fixed Remote Control failing to start from Claude Desktop when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK is set on a paid plan
  • Fixed model switches, messages and interrupts waiting behind a context usage check in SDK and desktop sessions
  • Fixed context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted errors behind LLM gateways; Claude Code now resends the request without that field
  • Fixed OpenTelemetry settings delivered through server-managed settings being ignored for the whole session after signing in during first-run setup or the first start after /logout

blogs.title: v2.1.302
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL to choose the model the client-side auto mode classifier uses; it does not change the model for server-side auto mode
  • Added an Idle compaction row to /config for turning idle compaction off or back on; the notices shown after an idle compaction now say how to turn it off
  • Added a notice to /design-sync and /design-login that standalone Claude Design (claude.ai/design) closes by December 14, 2026
  • Fixed a "Prompt is too long" error when stopping a turn while the conversation was being compacted
  • Fixed requests failing with "diagnostics: Extra inputs are not permitted" after switching to Vertex or Bedrock mid-session
  • Fixed the Read tool loading an image file of any size, or a pipe or device named like an image, entirely into memory; image sources over 128 MB are now refused
  • Fixed /autocompact and /effort saving to the wrong model when a gateway names Opus 4 or 4.1 with a prefix, such as anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
  • Fixed a prompt cache miss when a tool added mid-session was loaded again through ToolSearch or after compaction
  • Fixed claude plugin and other subcommands sometimes exiting before a queued settings or config write finished, which could lose the change or leave a .tmp file behind
  • Fixed plugin marketplaces re-cloning on every refresh, and newly installed git plugins showing version "unknown", when git defaults to the reftable ref format
  • Fixed the PowerShell tool not finding commands in a plugin's bin/ folder, and reporting an error when a search that finds nothing (rg, grep, findstr, git grep) is piped into Select-Object or another formatting cmdlet
  • Fixed Claude in the desktop app pointing you to claude.ai settings or /mcp to authorize or reconnect an MCP server where that option isn't available
  • Fixed artifact publishes sometimes failing when Claude sent an empty list of edits, and Claude retrying an artifact update the wrong way after a newer version of the artifact turned it away
  • Fixed classifier_category missing from OpenTelemetry tool_decision events for most auto mode classifier blocks, and new tool_decision attributes pushing out tool_use_id, tool_source and tool_parameters when OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT is low
  • Fixed rows in the agents view staying blank after moving down a long list or folding a section
  • Fixed claude remote-control --help not printing its usage and exiting when not signed in
  • Fixed /design consent and /design revoke suggesting /design-login when they fail in a cloud session, where it isn't available; the message now points to claude.ai/design/settings
  • Fixed MCP servers showing no tools, or every tool call failing, when the server negotiates protocol version 2026-07-28 but omits resultType, ttlMs or cacheScope
  • Fixed prompt suggestions spending usage credits on models your plan pays for only with credits: they are now skipped after a reply billed to credits
  • Fixed URLs written in backticks being clickable only on their first row when they wrap; the whole URL is now one link in terminals that support hyperlinks
  • Fixed claude plugin details @builtin suggesting claude plugin list, which never shows built-in plugins, when the plugin isn't found; it now points to /plugin
  • Fixed an emoji that a link starts inside wrapping one column too wide, which hid it in question previews and turned tables into lists
  • Fixed worktree isolation refusing to create or resume

blogs.title: v2.1.301
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_MAX_USAGE_LIMIT_WAIT_MS so unattended retry mode (CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG) ends a request at a usage limit that resets too far away instead of waiting
  • Added OpenTelemetry tracing guidance to the claude-api skill, including setting up trace destinations with the ant CLI
  • Added the % motion to vim mode: jump to the matching bracket, alone or with d/c/y
  • Added rows to a mod's Input: a text field of several lines in the terminal, where Enter submits and Shift+Enter or a backslash before Enter starts a new line
  • Added classifier_verdict and permission_mode to OpenTelemetry tool_decision events, so auto mode classifier decisions can be told apart from permission rules
  • Added classifier_category to OpenTelemetry tool_decision events, naming the built-in rule a classifier block matched, when OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1
  • Fixed quitting removing a worktree made by a WorktreeCreate hook without asking when it may hold unpushed commits
  • Fixed the fable (and best) model alias erroring on the Anthropic API when the newest Fable model is not available to your organization: Claude Code now retries once on the previous Fable model
  • Fixed a misleading "Please run /login" error when a full disk keeps the login from being refreshed; the error now names the disk and says to delete files
  • Fixed Grep and Glob reporting no matches when the search program failed unexpectedly before returning any results; they now return an error saying the search failed
  • Fixed workflow agents sometimes skipping their step, and the run still reporting success, after reading the harness note that their task text carries no user authority
  • Fixed artifact updates being refused where a PreToolUse hook covers Edit or Write; Claude now edits the file and then republishes instead of changing it in the publish call
  • Fixed skills and commands with very many or very long argument names stalling for seconds when invoked; only the first 64 names, each up to 64 characters, are now filled in
  • Fixed skills, commands and hooks using very large amounts of memory when their arguments fill many placeholders
  • Fixed stray characters such as >0q covering the folder trust prompt, and >4m before the shell prompt at exit, in terminals built on VTE older than 0.53 such as MATE Terminal on RHEL 8
  • Fixed stray GOK text appearing in the prompt at startup in some versions of iTerm2
  • Fixed switching to a model whose name contains application-inference-profile running your awsAuthRefresh command and delaying model-switch hooks when the provider is not Bedrock
  • Fixed sign-in refresh timeouts and unexpected sign-outs after a short command such as claude auth status or claude plugin list exited in the middle of a token refresh
  • Fixed a tool call cut off by a message sent mid-turn during its permission check being reported to the model as rejected by the user
  • Fixed a case where switching to a model with a smaller context window could spend usage credits on a summary by the previous model without asking first
  • Fixed conversations being compacted over and over, on a model you didn't pick, behind an LLM gateway whose responses name a different model than the one requested
  • Fixed vim mode sometimes staying in INSERT after Escape on a slow or busy machine
  • Fixed Esc discarding a typed AskUserQuestion answer in vim mode: the free-text field now supports vim NORMAL mode, and Esc cancels only from NORMAL
  • Fixed the Read tool reading binary files such as .xlsm, .parquet, .e

blogs.description: Authenticate MCP servers from your shell with claude mcp login, get a response to shell mode command output with the ! prefix, and resume a conversation from before /clear with /rewind.
blogs.content: What's New Week 26 · June 22–26, 2026 Copy page Copy page Authenticate MCP servers from your shell with claude mcp login, get a response to shell mode command output with the ! prefix, and resume a conversation from before /clear with /rewind. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.185 → v2.1.193 2 features · June 22–26 Authenticate MCP servers from the CLI v2.1.186 New claude mcp login <name> and claude mcp logout <name> commands authenticate a configured MCP server from your shell instead of the interactive /mcp menu. claude mcp login runs the server’s OAuth flow directly, and claude mcp logout clears the stored credentials. Run the OAuth flow for a configured server without opening a session: terminal claude mcp login sentry Authenticate from the command line Shell mode responds to command output v2.1.186 Commands you run with the ! prefix now get a response from Claude once the output lands in the transcript, so you can run ! npm test and get an explanation of the failures without a second prompt. The response costs the same as sending a normal prompt. To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json . Run a command and get a response to its output: Claude Code > ! npm test Shell mode with the ! prefix Other wins /rewind can now resume a conversation from before /clear was run New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables Org-configured model restrictions now apply to the model picker, --model , /model , and ANTHROPIC_MODEL , with a “restricted by your organization’s settings” message when a restricted model is selected New autoMode.classifyAllShell setting routes all Bash and PowerShell commands through the auto-mode classifier, and denial reasons now show in the transcript, the denial toast, and /permissions New claude_code.assistant_response OpenTelemetry log event carries the model’s response text; deployments that already log prompt content start receiving it on upgrade, so set OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0 to keep prompts only Background subagents now surface permission prompts in the main session instead of auto-denying; the dialog shows which agent is asking, and Esc denies only that tool /install-github-app can now install only the GitHub App and skip the Actions workflow and secret steps Hosts you allow in the sandbox network permission dialog are remembered for the rest of the session instead of re-prompting on every connection Streaming responses use about 37% less CPU, and long-session memory growth from the terminal output cache is reduced /review <pr> now uses the same review engine as /code-review medium Bash mode ! commands get live file path autocomplete Full changelog for v2.1.185–v2.1.193 → Was this page helpful? blogs.content: What's New Week 25 · June 15–19, 2026 Copy page Copy page Publish a live, shareable page from your session with Artifacts, match tool parameters in deny and ask rules, and set any setting from the prompt with /config. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.178 → v2.1.183 3 features · June 15–19 Artifacts An artifact is a live, interactive page that Claude Code publishes from your session to a private URL on claude.ai, and it updates in place as the session keeps working. Ask for one when terminal text is the wrong medium, such as a PR walkthrough with the diff annotated inline or a dashboard built from session data. Artifacts are in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Ask Claude for a page, then approve the publish prompt: Claude Code Make an artifact that walks through this PR with the diff annotated inline. Create an artifact Match by input parameter v2.1.178 Deny and ask permission rules can now match a tool’s input parameters with the Tool(param:value) syntax. For example, Agent(model:opus) matches subagent spawns that request the Opus model tier. The value accepts * as a wildcard, so Agent(isolation:*) matches any explicit isolation value. Add a parameter rule to the deny list in settings.json : .claude/settings.json { "permissions" : { "deny" : [ "Agent(model:opus)" ] } } Match by input parameter Set any setting from the prompt v2.1.181 Pass key=value to /config to change a setting directly without opening the Settings interface. The syntax also works in non-interactive mode with the -p flag and from Remote Control. Set the thinking setting from the prompt: Claude Code /config thinking=false Commands reference Other wins Auto mode now blocks destructive git commands ( git reset --hard , git clean -fd , git stash drop ) when you didn’t ask to discard local work, and blocks terraform destroy unless you asked for the specific stack Set the new attribution.sessionUrl setting to false to omit the claude.ai session link from commits and PRs in web and Remote Control sessions In the /config interface, Enter and Space both change the selected setting, and Esc now saves and closes instead of reverting New sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS Point CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE at a marker file to suppress mobile push notifications while you’re at the machine Long paragraphs now stream line by line instead of waiting for the first line break API connection drops mid-thinking now retry automatically instead of showing “Connection closed while thinking” With CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 set, every session has one implicit team, so you spawn teammates directly with the Agent tool’s name parameter Skills in nested .claude/skills directories load when working on files there; on a name clash the nested skill appears as <dir>:<name> so both stay available Fixed prompt caching not reading on a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and on Microsoft Foundry Fixed Write and Edit producing zero-byte or truncated files on network drives and cloud-synced folders Full changelog for v2.1.178–v2.1.183 → Was this page helpful?
